context: O-lan, a devoted wife and mother, is nearing the end of her life and is determined to see her son married and settled before she dies. Wang Lung, her husband, is struggling to cope with her illness and is trying to reassure her that everything will be alright.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening_third.speaker: Wang Lung
opening_third.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening_third.speaker: Wang Lung
opening_third.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
